hints: Focus on the central atom at each angle and count how many sigma bonds and lone pairs it has, as this controls the shape.
Notice that x is around N with three bonds and one lone pair, while y is around C with four single bonds.
Compare a pyramidal angle near 107 degrees, a tetrahedral angle near 109.5 degrees, and a trigonal planar angle near 120 degrees to order x, y and z.
walkthrough:
**Identify the environment of x**

Look at the left hand $\text{-NH}_2$ group. The N has three $\sigma$-bonds (two to H, one to C) plus one lone pair.

That is 4 electron pairs, pyramidal shape:
$$\text{bond angle x} \approx 107^{\circ}$$

**Identify the environment of y**

Look at the $\text{-CH}_2\text{-}$ carbon next to N. The C has four $\sigma$-bonds (to N, to C, to two H) and no lone pairs.

That is tetrahedral shape:
$$\text{bond angle y} \approx 109.5^{\circ}$$

**Identify the environment of z**

Look at the ring C joined to the side chain. It has three $\sigma$-bonds (to $\text{CH}_2$, to N, to C) with one $\pi$-bond, so it is $sp^2$.

That is trigonal planar shape:
$$\text{bond angle z} \approx 120^{\circ}$$

**Order from smallest to largest**

Now just compare the three typical values. Lone pair repulsion makes x the smallest.

$$107^{\circ} (x) < 109.5^{\circ} (y) < 120^{\circ} (z)$$

options.A: Correct. x is about 107 degrees (pyramidal N with lone pair), y is about 109.5 degrees (tetrahedral C), z is about 120 degrees (trigonal planar sp2 C). So x < y < z.
options.B: Incorrect. This puts y smaller than x. Students choose this if they forget the lone pair on N squeezes the H-N-H angle below the tetrahedral angle.
options.C: Incorrect. This puts z in the middle and x largest. It reverses the key ideas, treating the amine as larger than trigonal planar and the sp2 centre as smaller than tetrahedral.
options.D: Incorrect. This puts z smallest and x largest. Students choose this if they confuse double bonds with smaller angles, when in fact sp2 trigonal planar gives the largest angle here at about 120 degrees.
